reviews.text: This deliberately mischievous mix and each act’s limberly acrobatic flip ensures The Handmaiden keeps a tight grip on our attentions. Magnificent performances all round ensure our eye is pulled not just by their flesh, but also by their knotty intentions.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: The performances, the score, the craftsmanship, it’s all impeccable...
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Fiercely intelligent, unapologetically erotic and endlessly stylish, The Handmaiden is a perfect film that toys with the audience’s expectations and formed beliefs.
reviews.author: Diana Tuova

reviews.text: Park Chan-wook’s neurotic period piece is a beyond tricky weaving of conflicting identity, the desire for intimacy, masculinity vs. femininity, and historical and cultural oppression.
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: Park demonstrates how the complicated relationship between role-play, desire, secrecy, power and revenge prove ripe for darkly comic (and perverse) fodder.
reviews.author: Demitra Kampakis

reviews.text: Beautiful images in the frame with a grotesc story about the survival in a context war.  You have to watch it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: It’s a beautiful film of quality and cleverness.
reviews.author: Merryn Johns

reviews.text: Park Chan-wook's The Handmaiden envelops the viewer in a clever con game of psychological duplicity, depraved predators, dark humor, and sordid sexual delights.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: While its a feat of technical brilliance and visual genius, its the way Park uses his story to force his audience to question their assumptions that made me speechless the first time I saw it.
reviews.author: Daisy Leigh-Phippard

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is a remarkably progressive film that, despite using and abusing sex for the most part, refuses to objectify its subjects.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: Through the extremity of the story, Park manages to present a number of social messages, once more
reviews.author: Panos Kotzathanasis

reviews.text: Whether you've seen it before or not, now's as perfect time as any to see what all the fuss is about while [director director Park Chan-Wook] begins filming his upcoming his romantic murder mystery Decision to Leave this year.
reviews.author: Toussaint Egan

reviews.text: The drama combines the sumptuous art direction and black humor of Park's past work with a warmth and compassion that feeds the soul.
reviews.author: Li Sian Goh

reviews.text: A complicated revenge story, ripe with detail and secrets.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is an epic illustration that there is perhaps nothing more human than inhumanity.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: The twists in The Handmaiden come fast and furious. It's an engrossing tale that will constantly have you guessing which direction the narrative is headed.
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: Plenty of humor and an incomparably depraved, unyielding, violent, rebellious level of creativity.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: ...the love between the two lead women is what drives this film.
reviews.author: Casey Cipriani

reviews.text: Throbbing with greed and passion, deception and betrayal, the story remains every bit as gripping on screen as it was on the page.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: A rapturously seductive slow burn watch.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: "[Park]'s clearly a believer in the Roger Ebert school of thought, which favors appreciation over deconstruction."
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: "[Park]'s clearly a believer in the Roger Ebert school of thought, which favors appreciation over deconstruction."
reviews.author: Sarah Gorr

reviews.text: After witnessing this spectacle of eroticism and betrayal, we officially confirm that there is Park Chan-wook's cinema for a while. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is ambitious, hypnotic, and elegantly constructed, even with all of its countless twists and misdirections.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: A consuming love story blessing its audience with a memorable erotic scene involving a sharp tooth and a thimble.
reviews.author: Stefania Sarrubba

reviews.text: As we discover its twists and turns, the movie proves to be a much less interesting story than it seemed to be in its wonderful first act. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: The result is enticingly giddy in its psychological corruption, both of the characters - it's a standard gas-lighting plot - and of audience expectation.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: This entertaining potboiler manages to satisfy those in the mood for a historically compelling escapist yarn.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: The visual design of The Handmaiden is itself borderline pornographic- which makes the movie pretty impossible to dislike.
reviews.author: William Schwartz

reviews.text: Park Chan-wook crafts a mysterious, imaginative, and stylish to a fault feature that defies expectations and ranks among the year's finest.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Intertwines lustful carnal scenes and tense artful schemes.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: It's a film that gradually reveals its many layers of deception, is always visually stunning, yet drops one of the most intriguing deceits of the original novel and its new third part where loose ends are tied up seems rather abrupt.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: Each frame a picture, the film-critic-turned-filmmaker has a stunning eye for specificity that is reflected in the urgent nuances of every camera movement, every prop, every look, every framing choice.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: What we're eventually left with is one long, depthless ode to structure.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: Park clearly delights in the occasionally ridiculous levels of decadence he heaps on this layer cake of deception and deceit, but "The Handmaiden" shows the filmmaker's genuine tenderness as a real, if tortured love story forms at its core.
reviews.author: Stephen Saito

reviews.text: Chan-Wook Park's latest masterpiece is a film that really fire on so many different levels of brilliance - incredibly sexy in some moments, astoundingly disgusting in others; strongly dramatic and then building in unbearable tension.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is not only one of Chan-wook Park's best films, it is also his funniest. Actress Kim Tae-ri is officially a star.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: It would be a shame to spoil any of the silky curves of the story but sufficed to say that silver bells aren't just for Christmas time in the city anymore.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: The consistently strong cast and the roving camera that gives you a wide-angle tour of a half-Victorian, half-Japanese mansion-and the sex and violence-keeps things moving for a two-and-a-half hour ride that never gets boring.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: The film on its own has enough intriguing atmosphere, great performances, production design, and style to recommend it on the whole, but The Handmaiden constantly flirts with being too much of a good thing.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: Once again Park finds himself immersed in a world of woman-driven intrigue, and like Stoker before it The Handmaiden is concerned with the power dynamics between women in what are contextually configured as sexually transgressive scenarios.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is a triumphant project, pacing its plot well in order to stay engrossing for the whole of its runtime, and creating a dark and twisted piece of cinema that is an imaginative take on an English Victorian-set novel.
reviews.author: Stephanie Watts

reviews.text: Like reading a Dickens novel (or indeed a Waters yarn) the pleasure lies in taking one's time, losing oneself in a world a long way from our own.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: May be silly and slight, but it often strikes the right nerve.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: ... Park Chan-wook does what all excellent filmmakers strive to do- create a technically engrossing and emotionally compelling story that resonates with its audience far after the credits are finished rolling.
reviews.author: Morgan Rojas

reviews.text: [Director] Park Chan-wook is a poet of the realm of the flesh.
reviews.author: Charles Mudede

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is, above all, a delightful exercise in changing perspectives and sympathies. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nando Salvá

reviews.text: A solid entry, a brutal Dickensian movie from South Korea.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: Park's compromise-a tastefully arranged melodrama with elements of kitsch-is as incoherent as it is fetching.
reviews.author: Angelo Muredda

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is a GORGEOUS film, wonderfully acted by its three leads, with a twisty plot that will, at least once, elicit real shock.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: It's stylish and both Kims are terrific, but it's a long slog.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: The plot is deliciously twisted, while perceptions and truths are consistently challenged.
reviews.author: Pamela Jahn

reviews.text: If technology is the great mirror of our era, Black Mirror as a television show is the long gaze into our own reflections.
reviews.author: Teo Bugbee

reviews.text: [The Handmaiden is] gorgeously shot and composed, audacious, and full of witty visual asides.
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: The stylized acting requires Min-hee Kim as Lady Hideko, Kim Tae-ri as Sook-Hee and Jung-woong Jo as Fujiwara to convey volumes with silence, glances, and gestures, and they succeed admirably.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is exemplary proof of Park's mastery, a high point from a director known for his purposeful aesthetic care, even in matters of overwrought sexual melodrama.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: It's a brilliantly dark ode to women's desire and autonomy: a subject that remains as pressing today as it was a century ago.
reviews.author: Charlotte Richardson Andrews

reviews.text: The tricksy plot streamlines and improves the final messy section of the source novel, to tease and mislead even the most astute viewer.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: ... the look of a lavish period drama, the elegance of an arthouse film, the complex plotting of an ingenious caper that only the movies could sustain, and the sex of a classy softcore picture.
reviews.author: Sean Axmaker

reviews.text: If one wasn't swayed by Oldboy or [Chan-Wook's] underrated English-language debut Stoker, The Handmaiden may be the one to convince audiences of this remarkable talent.
reviews.author: Stephen Porzio

reviews.text: A twisty, twisted, psycho-sexual thriller, in which, for all its explicit content, nothing is quite as it appears.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is sensuous rather than lurid, an erotic thriller with a sense of humour and more than a few twists up its sleeve.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is stylish, funny and daring enough to keep you gripped to the end.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: There are giddy pleasures to be found in this rip-roaringly ripe erotic thriller/melodrama from Oldboy director Park Chan-wook.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: An astonishing erotic melodrama.
reviews.author: Camilla Long

reviews.text: The claustrophobic richness of the world he (Park Chan-wook) creates... lingers in the mind more even than the plot. His film presents a cloistered, colonial system, burned down by women's lust and love.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: The result is a lush, silken, erotic, disturbing, beautifully photographed drama of betrayal and passion.
reviews.author: Kate Muir

reviews.text: The intrigue, shifting alliances, and twisted revenge? Delicious, pulpy fun. The male-gazey soft-core porn that undermines the female protagonists? Not so much.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: The urge for a second viewing struck me midway through the first.
reviews.author: Matthew Norman

reviews.text: A sprawling, elaborate and labyrinthine tale of intrigue and deception, told as a battle of wills between the sexes, this is a glorious journey through the darker recesses of human desire.
reviews.author: Rob Daniel

reviews.text: The whole enterprise is presented with such breathtaking panache, intricacy and humour that it's impossible to resist.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Sexy, beautiful and constantly surprisingly, The Handmaiden is a satisfying period drama.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: In this hyper-intricate construction of false leads and surprise reversals, the ultimate dupe - and a very willing one - is the viewer.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: It is certainly a brilliant adaptation of Sarah Waters' original novel and a film about something that most other movies can only guess at: pleasure and rapture.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Lushly photographed, dizzyingly erotic thriller-slash-love story that's full of delicious twists and turns.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: A complex and wonderfully decadent erotic melodrama.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Plots twist and twist again, but the true surprise is the film's grasp of power between classes, and sexes, colonial and colonised. Nestled here too is a charge of real emotion.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A ravishing period piece that simmers with sexual tension while pulling off some dazzling narrative gymnastics.
reviews.author: Jordan Farley

reviews.text: A genuinely fun blend of sumptuous visuals and a perverse sense of humour.
reviews.author: Abbey Bender

reviews.text: Much as Lady Hideko's house is a clash of Western and Japanese architecture that somehow coalesces, so The Handmaiden mixes classical, formal composition with Park's typically twisted cinematic outlook.
reviews.author: Michael Bonner

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is at once a superlative thriller and a deeply erotic character study, but it's the intelligence, mordant wit and depth of characterisation that are the real turn-ons.
reviews.author: Andrew Lowry

reviews.text: A gloriously sensual and impressively layered thriller that's every bit as Hitchcockian and gothic as its predecessor.
reviews.author: Britt Hayes

reviews.text: [Park] has taken what could have been an ordinary and genteel costume drama and transformed it into an electrifying work that is in equal parts smart, bizarre, darkly funny, violent, powerfully acted and genuinely erotic.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: There's clearly an audience for this kind of high-concept erotic twaddle, but if Park changes tack for his next film, I won't complain. He's having fun here; he's also only a few shades away from E.L. James.
reviews.author: James Hadfield

reviews.text: Perhaps not since 'Pulp Fiction' have I seen such a cleverly convoluted story woven together from different perspectives. Act two and three pile on more layers of detail, adding more richness to the story.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Like everything by Korean auteur Park Chan-wook, The Handmaiden is meticulously controlled in form and bonkers-crazy in content. That's a heady combo.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Intelligent, absorbing and erotic.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: It combines Chan-wook's best obsessions: his aesthetic virtuosity, his dark sense of humor, his interest of sex as an unstoppable force and his characters penchant for vengeance. [Full review in Portuguese.]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: Fan of [Park's] will no doubt be sucked in by the distinct style, cinematography, and lush colors.
reviews.author: Charline Jao

reviews.text: A wonderfully twisted web of rococo theatrics, melodramatic twists, and deliciously lurid storytelling.
reviews.author: Witney Seibold

reviews.text: Even the most sensational sequences in The Handmaiden fail to do much more than disrupt the plot line.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: The ending doesn't live up to what precedes it, but while it's working, this is some of the most captivating and effective cinema of 2016, or indeed any of the last several years.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: The Handmaiden may not be the most concise effort we've seen from Chan-Wook as a director, but it's still an absolute masterpiece all the same.
reviews.author: Heather Wixson

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is a melodrama that delivers on its twists and turns.
reviews.author: Mal Vincent

reviews.text: Although The Handmaiden could easily rest on its violent, sexy laurels, Park and what must have been an army of set decorators, prop masters and costumers have created a dense, fully-realized world.
reviews.author: Stephen Danay

reviews.text: ...the more we unfold of its mystery, the deeper we fall into suspicion, desire, and depravity.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: A relentlessly beautiful film and one of the decade's most exhilarating and satisfying love stories.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: The triangle that ensues is voraciously sexual, unabashedly fetishistic. And the crosses, and the double-crosses, and the twists-within-twists are almost as carnal in their voluptuousness.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: An atypically swoon-worthy Park Chan-wook creation, he spins the script's elaborate gears to craft an alluring parable on oppressive class and gender roles.
reviews.author: Gary Shannon

reviews.text: An intricate story that mixes Gothic melodrama with the folklore of revenge and the libertine novel. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Costa

reviews.text: Narratively complex and scabrously amusing, The Handmaiden remakes the period epic into a study of personal power told through both sexual and colonial politics and batty heist flick diversions.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is Park Chan-Wook's best directorial effort since Oldboy, a near perfect blend of awesome visual style and engaging narrative.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: An excellent film that knows how to use the surprises to elevate everything else instead of compensating for possible shortcomings. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: A film that stands out for its perversion, protagonists, tempo, narrative tricks, and that modulates the question of how to be able to dominate the flow of glances. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Paula Arantzazu Ruiz

reviews.text: Sexy, sly "Handmaiden" a fun piece of deception.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: It's undoubtedly a masterpiece.
reviews.author: Christopher Schobert

reviews.text: A fascinating tale of deception and double-crosses.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: A visually exuberant film with a seductively perverse story that takes us from the exciting curiosity of the beginning to a growing and sustained perplexity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pilar Ayuso

reviews.text: One of the best, most unexpected movies of the year.
reviews.author: Rebecca Pahle

reviews.text: Go see it. If you love cinema at all, go see it.
reviews.author: Tom Long

reviews.text: A human drama loaded with love, passion, libido and social problems, where its director reinvents himself. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Felipe Tapia

reviews.text: Every shot is stunning, and many are breathtaking ... With its twisty-turny plot, stunning visuals and lashings of explicit lady-on-lady sex, [it] is probably [Park's] most accessible film to date. Great fun and an experiential feast.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: While "Oldboy" contained a whopper of a twist, "The Handmaiden" tells its story in more measured strokes, and yet is no less lurid or powerful.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Love conquers all in this beautiful movie, but it's not pretty.
reviews.author: Jay Stone

reviews.text: Chan-wook [delivers] a marvel of storytelling sleight of hand worthy of euphoric admiration.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Park chan-wook is brilliant in conveying a subtle and quiet tale of running from pain and sadness, while injecting much of what makes his films stand out from every other auteur working today.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: This nasty, perverted, and highly enjoyable erotic thriller is the most ferocious movie about matters of the heart since Dangerous Liaisons.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: One of the year's more delightfully offbeat and pleasurable films.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: Far too good to be watched in one sitting.
reviews.author: Tirdad Derakhshani

reviews.text: Chan-wook Park's The Handmaiden is deliciously perverse, delightfully twisty, and unapologetically erotic.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: this is film that should not be taken lightly. It will seep into the dark places of your psyche, and titillate your moral compass in disturbing yet delightful ways.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: A rich, intoxicating epic of chicanery and deceit-a puzzle that entangles the viewer just as it does its characters.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: A conspicuously crafty tale...Park's erotic thriller...with its story that, not coincidentally, deals with fetishes-never feels lifelessly premeditated; rather, we realize, early and often, that we are in very sure hands.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: The most sexually charged movie of the year.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is just pure cinema, a dizzying, disturbing fable of love and betrayal that piles on luxurious imagery, while never losing track of its story's human core.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Elegant and erotic, an elusive, yet exquisite example of sybaritic Asian cinema.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The flourishes of brutality, the pageantry of hardcore, the punchlines and slapstick gags: what's all this doing in an otherwise earnest film about deception and love?
reviews.author: Calum Marsh

reviews.text: Park Chan-wook is a master of classy trash... There's artistry in his filmmaking, but also a lot of blood, plenty of sick humor and moments of sheer lunacy. The Handmaiden ranks among his best films yet.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Twisted tale from Chan-wook Park is Korean hybrid Gothic pleasure.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: The surface is classical, while Park's perversity bubbles up from beneath.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: It holds its rapturous tease over us with scrumptious visuals, artful poise and dips into kink and gore that would give the Marquis de Sade reason to smile.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Kinky by design, artful by intent, the film draws visual inspiration from Gothic erotic art while distilling its screenplay - Chung Seo-kyung and Park share co-script - from the Sarah Waters Victorian crime novel Fingersmith.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Park Chan-wook's elegantly mounted Gothic story surprisingly combines sensuous melodrama and a delightfully full-blown romanticism.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: A bit too long and too twisty, but this is a beautifully mounted a large-scale epic drama. (Broad Street Review)
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Just when we figure out where it's going, it goes somewhere else. Just when we think it won't dare go somewhere, it does.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Co-writer/director Chan-wook Park's The Handmaiden is an invigorating exercise in shifting perspectives and sympathies.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Park's Handmaiden is a great big chocolate box of a movie in which a rich and satisfying narrative is enlivened by some piquant erotica and the sharp tang of politics.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: A sexy, stylish, surprisingly intelligent thriller that demands to be seen at least twice.
reviews.author: Tom Clift

reviews.text: "The Handmaiden" is 145 minutes of clever, erotic entertainment.
reviews.author: Bill Stamets

reviews.text: You have to stay on your toes while watching The Handmaiden. Like each of its central characters, Park Chan-wook's nimble erotic thriller has an agenda. And the South Korean auteur is always one step ahead of you.
reviews.author: T'Cha Dunlevy

reviews.text: While The Handmaiden is an empirically gorgeous movie no matter what's happening on screen, it also has no business being two-and-a-half hours long. It loses its momentum in the third act -- but lordy, those first two acts.
reviews.author: Sherilyn Connelly

reviews.text: How seriously can we take the film's rejection of systematic male oppression when it so blatantly objectifies its women?
reviews.author: Noah Gittell

reviews.text: It's a fine effort from a justifiably lauded creative force who lives to toy with his audience, often employing gruesome developments to do so.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Uncomfortable squirms, not titillation, seem the only reasonable response to ... the whole point of the movie.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: It may not be what viewers expect from Park Chan-wook -- it's even better.
reviews.author: Laura DeMarco

reviews.text: An engaging and evocative thriller/love story, The Handmaiden is ultimately a tale of freedom and transformation, as satisfying as an exquisitely choreographed four-course meal.
reviews.author: Josh Kupecki

reviews.text: Everything in "The Handmaiden" is ripe, sensual, rich. There's no beauty in chopping off fingers, it's true. But it can be artfully done.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: There may not be a director currently working who's more of an evil genius, or whose movies offer more double-edged delights.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: "The Handmaiden" is a fever dream from South Korean virtuoso Park Chan-wook, bursting with the kind of goodies that send cinephiles into ecstasy.
reviews.author: Walter V. Addiego

reviews.text: You have, I promise, never seen a movie quite like Park Chan-wook's "The Handmaiden."
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is an undeniably lush, meticulously constructed film whose celebration of perversity is among the most artful you'll see.
reviews.author: Walker MacMurdo

reviews.text: A shot of both beauties from behind, their hair in twin twists, feels like Park playing to porn fantasies. Yet he respects them as individuals, even when we're not sure who they really are
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: A deliciously black-humored erotic thriller ... with sex scenes so steamy and cruelty so gratuitous that you have to smile at the filmmaker's cheerful perversity.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: "The Handmaiden" hails from South Korea, but compared to most American movies of its scale and budget, it might as well have been made on another planet.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: Despite its flaws, the Handmaiden is worth a watch for its complex female characters, its captivating plot, and the gorgeous costumes and scenery.
reviews.author: Erika W. Smith

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is a nearly flawless movie. Every frame, every movement of the camera, every performance feels perfectly calibrated for maximum effect.
reviews.author: Emily St. James

reviews.text: 'The Handmaiden' delivers a spellbinding tale of love, betrayal and revenge.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: The level of craft is so consistently high that it's impossible to be anything less than entertained.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: The film runs nearly two-and-a-half-hours, but that's just the right amount of time for Park to turn up the heat a few degrees at a time.
reviews.author: Keith Phipps

reviews.text: While it's shallow and melodramatic, there's also an intoxicating quality to the imagery and the storytelling that keeps it compelling throughout.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Absolutely gorgeous, with so much attention paid to every visual detail from the costumes to the mansion's many rooms.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Like Park's best work, it's an expressionistic, at times surreal movie that skates along the knife-edge of dreams. Every frame pulses with life, sometimes with blood.
reviews.author: Matt Zoller Seitz

reviews.text: This breathless feminist thriller has the refined style of an art film but offers the disreputable fun of a guilty pleasure.
reviews.author: John Powers

reviews.text: the fine art of erotic manipulation is gleefully on display
reviews.author: Emma Myers

reviews.text: With this astonishing adaptation Chan-wook has taken his unique blend of brutality, beauty, humor and heart to dizzying new heights.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Like a Victorian settee infested with vipers, Park Chan-wook's The Handmaiden mixes the elegant and the dangerous, the refined and the venomous; it affects refinement and crawls on its belly. It's also apt to bite.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: The art of the tease is rarely as refined as in "The Handmaiden."
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Eschewing his usual modus operandi for the rollicking tension of active kink, Park finds a percolating balance between sensuality and sin, and it might just win him admirers beyond the usual bloodthirsty fanboys.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: A teasingly witty and elegant puzzle-box of a thriller whose pleasures are rooted not in visceral shock but in narrative surprise, and which wisely opts to seduce rather than pulverize its audience.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: The tasteful and the trashy make acrobatic bedfellows in Park Chan-wook's "The Handmaiden," a movie so assured it can do a sex scene where the camerawork is as arresting as the bodies engaged in combat.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: Both actresses deliver vivid, tender performances; they generate all the movie's fire, but they're obliged to do it inside a chilly, ritualized framework, the aesthetic equivalent of a softcore mausoleum.
reviews.author: Laura Miller

reviews.text: [The Handmaiden,] Park Chan-wook's Korean- and Japanese-language take on Welsh novelist Sarah Waters's Victorian-set romantic thriller Fingersmith, may be the best adaptation of this year. It is certainly the most innovative.
reviews.author: Lisa Rosman

reviews.text: Park seizes on the story's potent combination of larceny and taboo sexuality, and his steamy love scenes are enhanced by Seong-hie Ryu's sumptuous set decor.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: Lush, kinky, twisty and erotic, writer/director Park Chan-wook springs back from his gorgeous but emotionally anemic "Stoker," returning to the warped mind games, three act structure and cephalopod mollusc of "Oldboy"...a delirious cinematic experience
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Give Park the chance work you into a lather over the course of 145 minutes. There are few filmmakers on Earth capable of crafting the experience of movies like The Handmaiden so exquisitely while maintaining both plot inertia and a sense of fun.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: Director Park Chan-wook has always had a stunningly cinematic eye, but he's better known for gouging someone else's out. In The Handmaiden, he demonstrates a lightness and humor unseen in his previous work.
reviews.author: Kevin P. Sullivan

reviews.text: Sure, Park might be at Peak Male Gaze here, but he's also telling a dazzling, darkly comic story about two women fed up with the patriarchy.
reviews.author: April Wolfe

reviews.text: The Handmaiden, while a visually dazzling feast for the senses, seems to be on a mission to tell its already elaborate story in the most intricate fashion imaginable.
reviews.author: David Noh

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is a captivating and beautiful story of two underestimated women manipulating the manipulators.
reviews.author: Samantha Ladwig

reviews.text: Elegant, intensely romantic... The visual equivalent of drinking three glasses of champagne in the bath.
reviews.author: Tom Huddleston

reviews.text: The secret of the film, I suspect, is its love of secrets. The men and women guard their stratagems like jewels, and their lusts like hidden fires.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Few directors can so instantly draw your attention to the screen the way Park can.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Led by two fantastic lead performances, The Handmaiden is smart, sadistic and sexy as hell.
reviews.author: Peter Turner

reviews.text: With The Handmaiden, Park Chan-wook has made a gigantic leap as an artist, but he retreats to lurid cartoonishness just as he's earned your trust.
reviews.author: Chuck Bowen

reviews.text: Park Chan-wook's The Handmaiden is a chef-d'oeuvre of intrigue and erotica. It is a sumptuously artistic tale, exquisitely shot, that will leave you breathless.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: A bold, beautiful and way-out-there female revenge story that eschews the bloodless nature of most costume dramas to revel in the lusty passions, kinky hobbies and digit-dicing proclivities of its main characters.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Whether this is Park's best film is up for debate, but it could be in the running for your new favourite.
reviews.author: Adrian Mack

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is part romance, part gothic fairy tale and part psychosexual chamber piece, an initially beguiling film whose heavy-handed love scenes work to undermine its dramatic power.
reviews.author: Nikki Baughan

reviews.text: A darkly comic study in sex, class and Japanese-Korean relations.
reviews.author: Josh Slater-Williams

reviews.text: Park Chan-wook's The Handmaiden is for lovers: of others, of South Korean cinema and, most importantly, of psychosexual mind games. Finally, something for everyone.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Female leads Kim Min-hee and Kim Tae-ri are both standouts, conveying the complexity of the film's multi-layered con games with subtle changes of facial expression and tone of voice.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: The love scenes between Sook-hee and Hideko are beautiful, explicit, and funny, displaying a candor about sexuality that's not intended to shock but to draw you in-it's the most normal thing about this flamboyant, acerbic film.
reviews.author: Violet Lucca

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is another masterpiece from Park Chan-wook - a story of love, betrayal, and deceit that is beautiful, funny, romantic, and sexy.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: Park plays fast and loose with expectations, with a shape-shifting plot that's as ornate as the art direction- a mirrored dollhouse of seduction, deception and fatal attraction.
reviews.author: Brian D. Johnson

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is a sexy, seductive "thriller" that attempts to play the multiple-perceptions game, but misses on being a masterclass because of its daunting length.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: He's in such supreme command of his craft that to watch 'The Handmaiden' is to watch a man drunk on the joy of movie-making - and to share the same buzz.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: 'The Handmaiden' is thoughtful and complex while also being immensely entertaining, funny, dark, and disturbing.It's the kind of masterful work we've come to expect from Park Chan-wook.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: By replacing the class system of Victorian England with the dynamic of the occupier and occupied, Park has tapped into something uniquely complex about a chapter of history that is rarely explored.
reviews.author: Emily Yoshida

reviews.text: A pervy, picture-perfect period piece.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: Park goes all-out in series of gratuitous, nearly explicit, sex scenes. That's not in itself such a bad thing, but when he opts for a severely sadistic sequence near the end, he goes too far.
reviews.author: Susan G. Cole

reviews.text: An appealing world which has been built upon the bowels of Hell, a spectacular drama with fierce performances and fiery sensuality.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Park's adaptation of [Fingersmith] has its own unpredictability. And while it's still largely the same story, there are points where this new interpretation takes its own direction and charges ahead without so much as a look behind.
reviews.author: Melalin Mahavongtrakul

reviews.text: ... the film practically drips with fetishistic imagery and detail.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: One part Gothic fantasy, one part softcore thriller... blurs the line between highbrow and sexploitation so skilfully you will be left wondering if you just watched a big-budget skin flick or a particularly smutty arthouse production.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Billed by some as a lurid lesbian potboiler when it premiered in Cannes, The Handmaiden is much more lavish than this reductive description suggests.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: [CANNES 2016] Lush production designs and keen cinematography drink in dynamic performances (by Kim Min-Hee and Kim Tae-Ri) teeming with an urgent lesbian sensuality.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: The Handmaiden is sexy and twisty and so compelling despite this, lodging itself in the points of view of two women who are constantly underestimated by the men around them, and who learn to take advantage of how they're misjudged.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Practically every surface in the film screams fetish, and, as in his underrated Stoker, Chan-Wook locates eroticism in some unusual places.
reviews.author: Catherine Bray

reviews.text: ... the film is a handsomely opaque, overtly familiar, sexually evocative romance that never bores you and yet, throughout, I felt like something was missing.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: The Korean filmmaker makes a great comeback with his transgressive adaptation of one of the most notorious authors of homosexual fiction. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: An intelligent, funny erotic thriller, The Handmaiden seems destined for some kind of American remake... that isn't likely to live up to Park's invention, wit, and daring. See this one first, if you can.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Starts out looking as if it'll be a deeply serious (and seriously depressing) tale of a Korean "comfort woman" forced to service the occupying Japanese military. After about five minutes of grandiose solemnity, Park drops the charade.
reviews.author: Mike D'Angelo

reviews.text: Park has genre-ised this material right up with a lip-smacking, borderline pervy glee, but leaves us with relationships that only sketchily make sense.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Manages to surprise us in almost every scene, every frame.
reviews.author: Talia Soghomonian

reviews.text: The film is not all bad -and ensures another surprise at the end-, but by that time you'll be already tired of a story that might well have been resolved in 100 minutes without exaggerating the visual stylization. [Full review in spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Lerer

reviews.text: The Handmaid gives all the preciousness and virtuosity to the montage, framing and lighting that are the hallmark of the South Korean filmmaker. [Full review in spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: The imaginery used by Chan-Wook is both bright as dirty, as delicately as culpably exhibitionist voyeur. [Full review in spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: Park shows more subtelty and an obvious growth in his craft as a filmmaker. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Leonardo Garcia Tsao

reviews.text: The movie works, but in the end the idea of more style over matter lingers around. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: Chan-wook recreates in a stylish way all the parts of a story whose dramatic entity is much more elemental than what you can see at first glance. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos F. Heredero

reviews.text: Deliriously fun, terminally silly.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: Exquisitely designed and sexually liberating, this is a hugely entertaining thriller that has shades of Gaslight, Les Diaboliques and last year's Duke of Burgundy, but thankfully no grey.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: The film manages the tricky feat of both staying true to Waters breathless, page-turning prose, and creating a wholly persuasive new milieu for the story.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Clever, heady and sensually lavish to a fault.
reviews.author: Maggie Lee

reviews.text: All the best things about Asian cinema, rolled into one.
reviews.author: Deborah Young

reviews.text: It's slow to start, but once things start to move along and come together, the journey is riotous, depraved, and delightful.
reviews.author: Matt Hoffman

synopsis: With help from an orphaned pickpocket (Kim Tae-ri), a Korean con man (Ha Jung-woo) devises an elaborate plot to seduce and bilk a Japanese woman (Kim Min-hee) out of her inheritance.
